text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United States is having second thoughts about its initiative on Cyprus. Ambassador Kenneth Brill meets President Clerides today.
- Cyprus's accession process to the European Union will be in two stages if in the meantime the political problem is not solved.
- Israeli escapers are granted a mystery pardon less than three months into their sentence.
- Government tables bill to parliament to regulate company takeovers.
- Confusion reigns over Cyprus's position on a U.S. proposal to ban overflights.
- "Grey Wolves" threaten to move in to the abandoned resort of Varosha in the north.
- Athens seeks guarantees of Cyprus's security from the United States. Washington is continuing a dialogue on its proposal to ban military overflights through (ambassador) Brill.
- Top secret government documents on persons missing since 1974 have disappeared.
- A crisis between Disy and Diko parties in the government partnership is defusing.
- The government is expected to announce incentives to boost the stock exchange.
